posts.content: As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Use encounter outcomes as evidence, but treat public claims as unverified.
As good: cooperate with likely-good players to preserve joint welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Track each opponent’s actions and update beliefs.

I am good; maximize total good-player payoffs. Against likely good, cooperate (CC yields 6 good points); against likely selfish, defect (avoid giving them 5 while earning 5). Track encounters and calibrate beliefs; no evidence yet.
P10 is unknown. For a good opponent, C maximizes total good-player payoff regardless of their action; against a selfish opponent, D is safer. Track P10’s action and infer from evidence.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns us both 3. I encourage everyone to choose C when they meet me.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents when that improves good players’ total payoff. Prior: each other player’s selfish probability ≈0.291.

I’m good. Start cooperative with P2; record their action and payoff. Cooperate with likely good players to raise their joint good-player payoff; defect against likely selfish players, and use observed behavior to update beliefs.
No evidence yet about P1 or the leader. Favor cooperation absent contrary evidence; record P1’s action and payoff implications for future decisions.
As selfish, prioritize payoff: defect against likely cooperators; cooperate only if mutual cooperation improves expected returns.
P3 is unknown; cooperate absent evidence of defection.
P8 cooperated when I did, but one encounter is weak evidence. P10 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfish play, and record its action for updating.
P5 defected against my C without prior evidence; raise suspicion, but one encounter is not conclusive. P1 has no observed behavior. Against P1, C is best absent evidence of selfishness.

P10’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness. P6 publicly promises C; treat that as evidence but not proof. Against a likely good opponent, C improves total good-player payoff; against a likely selfish defector, D protects my own payoff.
I’m selfish and will defect against P7; unilateral defection pays more regardless of their action.
I’ll choose C when we meet this round. Mutual cooperation gives us both 3, so please cooperate too.
P6 promised C but chose D; treat that as evidence of selfishness. P5 has no encounter evidence yet.
P2 chose C against my C, strong evidence P2 is good: selfish players benefit from defecting. Cooperate with likely good players; update beliefs from future encounters.

Against a good player, C maximizes joint good-player payoff; against a selfish player, D earns me 5 while their payoff is excluded. Selfish players should always D, so record actions as evidence. With no evidence, favor C.
Round 2: defect against P2; in this one-shot payoff matrix D strictly dominates C regardless of their action.

P9 and P3 chose C against me, evidence they are likely good; P5 remains unknown. P6’s public cooperation claims are unverified. As good, favor C with likely-good opponents and D against likely-selfish ones.

P10 defected against my C: strong, though not conclusive, selfish evidence. P6’s repeated promise to cooperate is only a claim; judge by its action when observed. Against likely-good players, C supports good-player welfare; against likely-selfish players, D protects my payoff.
P5’s D against my C raises suspicion, but one action is weak evidence because good players may also defect. P1 cooperated. P10 is untested; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness.

P10 defected against my C; strong selfish evidence. P6 promised C but played D against me, also strong selfish evidence and undermines its public claims. Against P9, choose C if likely good, D if likely selfish.
Keep defecting: D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
I’ll cooperate when I meet P2; mutual C benefits us both. Everyone else, consider cooperating with your opponent too.
P6 and P5 both defected against my C; treat each as likely selfish. P8 is untested: cooperate to test, then update from their action.

I’m good. P2 and P9 cooperated, so treat them as likely good; P7 is unobserved. Against likely-good players, cooperate to maximize their joint good-player payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions; consider defection against likely selfish players.

Against good players, C maximizes joint welfare; against selfish players, D earns me more while their payoff is excluded. Selfish players should D. P1 and P8 cooperated with me, evidence they are good. P4 is unobserved; favor C absent contrary evidence.
P3 is an unseen one-shot opponent; choose D, which strictly dominates C regardless of their action.

P3 and P9 cooperated against me; P5 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness. P4 is untested. Favor C with likely-good opponents, D when selfishness is sufficiently likely; public claims remain unverified.

P5 is unobserved: cooperate to preserve joint welfare if likely good; defect if evidence suggests selfishness. P10’s D against C is strong selfish evidence; P8’s C supports good, though neither is certain. P6’s public promises are unverified.
P5 defected against my C; P10 chose D in D-D; P1 cooperated. P6’s repeated C assurances are cheap talk, but no encounter evidence yet. Judge by its actual action; favor C if P6 appears good.

P6 and P10 both defected against my cooperation; treat them as likely selfish, not certain. P1 is unobserved. For an unknown opponent, cooperate if the chance they’re good exceeds roughly 25%; update from actual encounters, not promises.
Defect against P2; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
I intend to cooperate with P3 this round; mutual C earns us both 3. Please reciprocate.
P5 and P6 defected against my C, so treat them as likely selfish; P8 reciprocated, weak evidence of being good. P9 is untested: cooperate, then update from their action.
P2, P9, and P7 each cooperated with me; that favors them being good. I’ll cooperate with P10 unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P1 and P8 cooperated, so treat them as good; update selfish probabilities among the remaining players accordingly. Selfish players should defect. Against P7, favor C absent evidence of selfishness; record their action.
P8 is an unseen one-shot opponent; defect maximizes payoff regardless of their action. Maintain uncertainty about their role until observing their move.

Good role. P3/P9 cooperated against my C; P4 cooperated against my D; P5 defected against my C, raising suspicion but not certainty. P6’s repeated public cooperation claims are unverified. For our encounter, weigh expected total good-player payoff; favor C absent strong evidence.
P10 and P5 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish. Against P9, cooperate absent evidence of selfishness; record the action and update beliefs.
P6 promised C then chose D against my C; raise suspicion substantially. P5 also defected against C. P10’s D-D is ambiguous. P4 is untested; absent evidence, favor cooperation.

P6’s prior defection against me is strong selfishness evidence despite its cooperative broadcasts. P10 also defected; P1 defected once. P3 is unobserved: favor C if likely good, D if likely selfish, and update from actual behavior.
P8 is unobserved so far. Defect: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P8’s action.
P1, I’ll cooperate when we meet this round. Mutual cooperation earns us both 3, so please choose C too.
P10 is untested; cooperate to preserve mutual gains if they’re good, then update from their action. P5 and P6 defected against my C, which raises suspicion but does not prove they’re selfish.

P10 defected against my C; this is evidence for selfishness, though a good player might defect if suspecting me. P2, P7, P9 cooperated. P5 is unobserved; choose based on prior and update from behavior.
P1, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated with me, so treat them as good. P2 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence otherwise, and update from its action.
Defect against P7; this is a one-shot encounter, and D strictly dominates C regardless of P7’s action.
P8 is untested; cooperate absent strong evidence they are selfish. Against a likely-good player, C maximizes the combined good-player payoff; reserve D for strong evidence of selfishness.

P3 is unobserved; absent evidence, C supports good-player welfare. P5 and P10 defected against my C, strong but not conclusive selfish evidence. P8 and P9 reciprocated C. P6’s public cooperation claims remain unverified.
P2 is untested; favor C absent encounter evidence. P5 and P6 defected against my C; P6’s repeated promises followed by D make its assurances unreliable. P10’s D-D is ambiguous.

P7 is unobserved. Cooperate if their selfishness probability is below about 0.5; otherwise defect. P10 and P6 defected against my C, while P1 also defected; P3 and P9 cooperated. P6’s broadcasts are not reliable evidence.
Defect against P10 to maximize my payoff; update my beliefs after observing their action.
P9, I’ll cooperate when we meet this round. Choose C too and we can both earn 3.
P4 is untested; cooperate to preserve mutual gains if they’re good. P5, P6, and P10 defected against my C, raising suspicion but not proving they’re selfish.

P10 and P5 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish. P2, P7, and P9 cooperated, favoring good. P1 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise, then update from their action.

P1, P2, P4, P7, and P8 are good: they cooperated with me. Given these observations, P6’s selfish probability is about 0.25 before considering its repeated public C promises; promises are weak, unverified evidence. If P6 cooperates, it is good; if it defects, it is selfish.
P5 is unseen. Defect this round; use the observed encounters to update beliefs, but remember actions and claims are not proof of anyone’s role.
P7 is untested. For the good-player objective, favor C absent strong evidence they are selfish; update from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.

P4 is unobserved; cooperate to support good-player welfare. P5 and P10’s defections against C suggest selfishness; reciprocation from P8, P9, and P3 supports good. Treat P6’s public promises as unverified.

P8 is untested; prior selfish probability is about 1/3. Cooperate: against any action by a good player this maximizes combined good-player payoff, while defect only benefits us against a selfish opponent playing D. Ignore P6’s public promises; judge by observed actions.

P2 is unobserved; use prior and remaining-count constraints, not leader P6’s promises. P1 and P10 defected against my C; P6 defected against me; P3 and P9 cooperated, and P7 chose C against my D. Against P2, favor C if likely good and D if likely selfish.
P6 repeatedly broadcasts cooperation promises; cheap talk, not proof of type. D remains payoff-dominant against any action.
P5, I’ll cooperate when we meet this round. Mutual C earns us both 3, so please choose C too.
P1 is untested. Cooperate to enable mutual gains if they are good; update from their action. Defection against my C is strong evidence of selfishness, not proof.

P5 and P10 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish. P2, P7, P9 cooperated, favoring good. Against an unobserved player, cooperate if selfishness probability is below 0.5; otherwise defect to limit good-player losses.
P6's D identifies it as selfish. P1, P2, P4, P7, P8 cooperated, so are good; I am good. Given the count prior, two of P3, P5, P10 are selfish. P10's selfish probability is 2/3; choose D against it.
Round 7 vs P9 is one-shot; choose D regardless of their action.

P2 is untested; cooperate absent strong evidence they are selfish. Against a likely-good player, mutual C benefits the good-player total; selfish players tend to D, so D is preferable only with substantial evidence of selfishness.
P1 is unobserved. Against likely-good players, C supports joint welfare; D is preferable against likely-selfish players. Use encounter evidence, not public promises, to judge.

P7 is untested; prior selfish probability is about 1/3. Good-good mutual C maximizes their combined payoff, but against a selfish D, our D earns 5 for good players while C earns 0. Weigh this tradeoff; P5/P6 D against my C are strong selfishness evidence, while P1/P2/P4/P8 cooperated.

P8 is unobserved. Against P8, cooperate if their selfishness probability is below 0.5; otherwise defect. P3, P7, P9, and P2 cooperated in my encounters; P1, P6, and P10 defected. Actions are evidence, not proof, since good players may defect when they suspect selfishness.

Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P9's actual behavior is unknown; public cooperation claims are cheap talk. Earlier C responses to my D suggest non-selfishness, while D responses provide some evidence of selfishness.
P10, I’ll cooperate when we meet this round. Mutual C earns us both 3; please reciprocate.
P3 is untested; cooperate to allow mutual gains if they’re good, and update from their action.

P4 is unobserved; cooperate only if evidence puts their selfishness probability below 0.5, otherwise defect. Cooperation with a good player yields 6 total good payoff versus 5 from unilateral defection; against a selfish defector, D/D preserves 1 for me.
P1, P2, P4, P7, P8 cooperated with me and are good. P6 and P10 defected; strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P5 is unobserved: favor C unless further evidence suggests otherwise.
Round 8 vs P6: choose D; their public cooperation promise is unverified, and D maximizes payoff either way. Keep reports consistent with observed behavior, not claims.
Good objective: cooperate with P10 absent direct evidence of selfishness; mutual C maximizes good-player total. P5’s defection is evidence, not certainty. Ignore unverified claims.

P5, P10, and P4 defected against my C; this is strong selfish evidence, though a good player might defect strategically. P1, P3, P8, and P9 reciprocated C. P7 remains unobserved: choose C absent evidence of selfishness; ignore unverified claims.

Against P9, weigh selfishness probability against the 1/6 threshold: C benefits both good players if P9 is good; D protects good-player welfare if P9 is selfish and defects. Use quota constraints and observed behavior, not leader promises.
P5 is unobserved; don’t treat P6’s promise as proof of P5’s role. Cooperate unless evidence makes P5 very likely selfish; update beliefs from actual encounters.
P4, I intend to cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation earns us both 3; please choose C too.
P8, I’ll cooperate when we meet this round. Choose C too and we can both earn 3.
P2 is untested. Favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness; update from their action.
P6’s repeated public promises are cheap talk; no encounter evidence yet. Assess their type using the prior, not claims, and choose based on expected good-player payoff.

P1, P2, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated with me; P6 and P10 defected against my C, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P5’s D against my D is ambiguous. P3 is unobserved: favor C unless its selfish probability is high; update from its action.
Round 9 vs P1 is one-shot; defect maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action. Keep role beliefs separate from action evidence.

P5 defected against my C before, so they're the strongest selfishness suspect. For the final encounter, weigh that evidence and favor D if it makes the good-player total higher; no future reciprocity remains.
P10 defected against my C earlier, strong selfish evidence; for this final encounter, D protects good-player payoff if selfish.
P9 defected against my C last round, which is evidence of selfishness but not proof. Consider that history when choosing; prioritize total welfare of good players.
P8 cooperated with me before, strong evidence they’re good; favor C again to maximize good-player welfare. Past D actions suggest selfishness but are not conclusive.
Final round: choose D against P1; they previously cooperated against my D, but D maximizes my payoff either way.
P7, I’ll cooperate this time. I know my earlier D against your C cost you; choose C and we can both earn 3.
P6 defected against my cooperation in round 1; with only this final encounter left, treat that as strong evidence of selfishness.
P4 previously cooperated, making them likely good. On this final encounter, choose C to maximize joint good-player payoff; update beliefs from their observed behavior, not public claims.
P3 cooperated against my D in round 9, identifying P3 as good. Choose C to maximize our combined payoff; no future rounds remain.
Final round against P2: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with unknown opponents when mutual cooperation benefits the good players overall; update identity beliefs using encounter outcomes and treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with a likely-good opponent to support joint welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and outcomes.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent to maximize good-player payoffs; defect against evidence of a selfish opponent.
As a good player, cooperate when expected gains to good players outweigh the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect each round: it strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff in every encounter.
Exploit a possible C for the higher payoff; against D, defecting limits my payoff to 1.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely good players to improve their joint payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and payoffs.
Cooperate to favor joint good-player welfare; track encounter behavior and adapt in later rounds.
Defect to maximize expected payoff in this one-shot encounter; update beliefs from observed behavior and messages, but treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with unknown opponents while likely-good; update beliefs from my encounters, treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support joint welfare; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; update suspicions from observed actions.
Defect against likely selfish opponents, whose dominant action is D; cooperate when an opponent is likely good to increase good players’ combined payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update beliefs using observed actions, treating a selfish player as choosing the strictly payoff-dominant action.
Defect to maximize my payoff: D earns more against C and limits losses against D. I treat P7’s observed cooperation as evidence they are not selfish.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is most likely; update beliefs from actions, especially P6’s broken promise.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to favor joint welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize expected payoff; treat public promises as unverified and retain prior identity beliefs.
Cooperate with P5: absent evidence they are selfish, mutual cooperation is better for the good players overall. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role; public claims remain unverified.
Cooperate with a likely-good opponent to support total good-player welfare; use observed actions to update identity beliefs.
Defect when the risk of exploiting a selfish opponent outweighs the welfare gain from mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P9: the remaining-player selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat P6 and P10’s observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect to maximize my payoff. Since P3 and P7 cooperated against my defection, treat them as non-selfish; otherwise retain the prior conditional on my selfish role.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against C and limits my loss against D. My public promise does not change the payoff incentives.
Cooperate with untested opponents to favor mutual benefit among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior, treating repeated defections as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: cooperation benefits good players together, and the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection is better. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to favor good-player welfare; observed cooperation identifies P1 and P8 as good. Update beliefs and adapt from future encounters.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; observed cooperation against my defection lowers P2 and P4’s selfishness probabilities. Treat messages as unverified.
Defect against opponents with a meaningful chance of being selfish; cooperate when evidence suggests they are good. Treat observed actions as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when expected welfare favors mutual cooperation; defect when evidence makes exploitation by a selfish opponent more likely. Treat promises as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate with P1, who remains unobserved and is more likely good than selfish. Cooperation supports good players’ shared objective; observed defections make P6 and P10 likely selfish.
Defect to maximize my payoff; P1, P3, and P7 cooperated against my defection, so I treat them as non-selfish and update the remaining identities from the conditioned prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. My prior public promise does not change the payoff incentives.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against cooperation as evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good players to improve total good-player payoff; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P7: prior encounters identify P1, P4, and P8 as good, while P7 remains more likely good than selfish. Update from observed actions; treat leader claims as unverified.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. Treat public promises as unverified; retain the identity evidence from P2 and P4 cooperating against my defection.
Cooperate with P6 absent strong evidence of selfishness; use observed actions to update identity beliefs, while treating public promises as weak, unverified evidence.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect only when evidence warrants it.

Cooperate with an untested opponent; mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff. Update suspicions from observed actions, treating defections against cooperation as evidence but not proof of selfishness.

Cooperate with unobserved P3: the current selfishness estimate is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat defections against my cooperation as evidence, but account for uncertainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff. The four players who cooperated against my defection are non-selfish; distribute the remaining posterior probability across the unobserved players.

Defect because it pays more against C and limits my loss against D. P2, P3, and P7 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish optimizers; I have no decisive identity evidence about the others.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against cooperation as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P5: their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player payoff. Treat repeated cooperation as evidence of good intent and P10’s defection as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare, and the opponent’s selfish probability is below one half. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat leader messages as unverified.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. Lowered selfishness estimates for P2, P4, and P8 after they cooperated against my defection; treat other evidence cautiously.
Cooperate with P8 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; treat repeated defections against cooperation as evidence of selfishness and update beliefs from encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; update suspicions from observed actions, treating defection as evidence but not proof of selfishness.

Defect against P7, whose estimated selfishness is near or above the threshold where defection improves expected welfare for good players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, while treating single encounters as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff. Update identity beliefs from observed play, treating cooperation against my defection as evidence of a non-selfish player; treat unverified messages as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Their C responses to my D rule out selfish optimization; P4’s prior D modestly raises my belief, while others remain uncertain.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; treat defections against C as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P1: they are unobserved and their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player payoff. Treat P5 and P10’s defections as evidence of selfishness; prior cooperation favors P2, P7, and P9.
Cooperate with P6: observed cooperation identifies P1, P2, P4, P7, and P8 as good; P6’s promises are unverified, but its selfish probability remains below one half. Update from future encounters.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. Keep prior identity estimates for unobserved players and treat public cooperation promises as unverified.
Cooperate with P7 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; treat defections against cooperation as evidence of selfishness and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize welfare among good players; update selfishness beliefs from observed choices, treating defection against cooperation as evidence but not proof.

Defect against P2: unobserved-player selfishness is elevated after accounting for the observed actions and the count prior. Cooperate with likely good players; treat observed actions as evidence, not certainty.

Defect to maximize my payoff. Cooperation against my defection strongly suggests a non-selfish opponent; P10’s defection is some evidence of selfishness. Treat P6’s repeated promises as unverified cheap talk.

Defect: it pays more against C and loses less against D. The observed C responses to my earlier D actions rule out selfish optimization; P4’s D modestly raises my belief, with the remaining uncertainty distributed among P4, P5, P8, and P10.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation may benefit good players; treat defections against C as strong but fallible evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P3: cooperation improves good-player welfare, and their selfishness probability is below the threshold for defection. Past defections raise suspicion of P5 and P10; cooperation favors P1, P2, P7, and P9.
Cooperate with P10 while its selfish probability is below one half; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Treat P6’s defection as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. P7’s cooperation against my defection lowers my estimate of their selfishness; retain other estimates and treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P2 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits the good players. Use encounter behavior to update identity beliefs, treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; use observed defections against C as evidence of selfishness and reciprocated cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Against an untested opponent, defect when the chance they are selfish exceeds the welfare threshold; update beliefs from observed actions, treating D against C as evidence but not proof.

Cooperate with unobserved P8: estimated selfishness is below the threshold where defection improves expected welfare for good players. Observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation is strong evidence of a good role.
Choose D because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Prioritize observed actions over unverified claims when updating beliefs.

Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either opponent action. The players who cooperated against my earlier defections cannot be selfish optimizers; the remaining uncertainty is among P4, P5, P8, and P10.

Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against C as strong but fallible evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P4: their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Past cooperation favors P1, P2, P7, and P9; defections raise suspicion of P5 and P10.

Cooperate with likely-good players, but defect when the chance of a selfish opponent makes the payoff to good players higher. Observed cooperation is strong evidence of good type; defections are suggestive, not conclusive.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. P6’s public cooperation promise is unverified; retain prior estimates for unobserved roles and treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P10 absent evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed encounters and treat public claims as unverified.
Defect against P7 because an unobserved opponent retains enough selfishness risk to justify protecting good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P9 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when both are good. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for the likely total number of selfish players.

Cooperate with unobserved P5: the players who cooperated in my encounters are good, and the observed defections make P1, P6, and P10 more suspect. Choose C when the opponent is likely good to maximize good-player welfare.

Choose D to maximize my payoff against either action. The five players who cooperated against my D are non-selfish; the remaining identity probabilities reflect the count prior, with some evidence from observed defections.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either action. The observed C responses to my earlier defections rule out selfish optimization; remaining uncertainty is among P4, P5, P8, and P10.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation can benefit good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against C as strong but fallible evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P6: their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves good-player welfare. Prior defections raise suspicion of P5 and P10; cooperation favors the others.
Cooperate with likely-good players when that maximizes good-player welfare; defect when selfish-opponent risk makes defection better. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. Update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions; P6’s false cooperation promise is evidence, not proof.
Defect in the final encounter: P5’s earlier defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat them as evidence rather than certainty.
Defect against P10 given its prior defection against my cooperation; cooperate with likely-good players and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against P9 given its prior defection against my cooperation; update identity beliefs from observed actions while prioritizing total payoffs of good players.
Cooperate with P8, who previously cooperated with me and is likely good. Update role estimates from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than certainty.
Choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action. Prioritize observed play over unverified claims; the players who cooperated against my D cannot be selfish.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either action. P7 previously cooperated against my D, ruling out selfish optimization; I defect to maximize my final-round payoff.
Defect against P6 given their prior defection against my cooperation and the final-round incentive to protect good players from a likely selfish opponent.
Cooperate with P4, whose past cooperation strongly favors them being good. The defections by P5, P6, and P10 against my cooperation are strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P3, whose C against my D is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes our combined good-player payoff.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action; beliefs reflect observed behavior, not unverified claims.

Cooperated with opponents absent strong evidence of selfishness, updated beliefs from encounter actions, and treated public claims as unverified. Defected against P5 in the final round after repeated defection evidence.
As a good player, I mostly cooperated to support joint welfare, while defecting against P10 and updating private identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperated with opponents who appeared good and defected when evidence suggested exploitation; updated private identity beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as less reliable than actual play.
